title: IBM ReRAM endpoint model with a 128-pulse write-verify cap
hypothesis: Reducing the maximum target-programming budget from 512 to 128 pulses removes long soft-bound chases and noise-selected late admissions while retaining the endpoint distribution of persistently reachable targets well enough to fit the deployment noise, failure, saturation, and cost models.
motivation: The completed v2 study showed that essentially every 512-pulse failure was outside the sampled device's persistent reachable window. A post-completion prefix analysis selected 128, rather than 64, as the first successor cap: 64 discarded a substantial reachable adaptive-controller tail, whereas 128 reduces the worst-case pulse/read loop by four while retaining most observed accepted prefixes. This successor is a new declared study and does not rewrite the immutable v2 evidence.

completion_criteria: All four arms complete the matched 41-target, half-step-tolerance, two-start, two-controller design on 1024 device identities with four repeats and a strict 128-target-pulse cap: exactly 671744 trajectories per arm and 2686976 trajectories total.
Every run records the production_short_cap128 execution profile, maximum_program_pulses=128, the unchanged construction/conditioning/programming seeds, and the same identity partitions as v2.
Trajectory and verify-event ledgers pass the exact integrity contract and preserve accepted, failed, saturated, non-finite, corrupt, apparent-endpoint, and persistent-endpoint outcomes.

The cap comparison reports success-rate change, accepted-prefix retention, pulse and verify savings, and endpoint-residual change separately for controller, preset, corruption mode, start, target, and persistent-reachability class.
The 128-pulse empirical kernel and separate failure, corruption, saturation, and cost models are emitted and compared with both the immutable 512-pulse v2 model and Wan-2022.

For every preset, corruption mode, controller, and start condition, the runtime fits a target-conditioned eight-bin piecewise-uniform accepted-residual density with a 0.5 pseudocount per bin and reports the same held-out coverage and normalized target-binned Wasserstein adequacy gates as the Gaussian model.

For every target and condition, paired persistent lower/upper boundary states classify each non-corrupt fit and validation trajectory as target-below-lower, target-inside-bounds, or target-above-upper; the report keeps exact reachability, verify-window intersection, and apparent acceptance separate and publishes fit-versus-validation class-probability error.
No HWA, Tiki-Taka, LoRA, or network-accuracy conclusion is drawn from this device-characterization study.
analysis_plan: Use the same seeds and device identities as v2 so the pulse cap is the only declared intervention; compare exact rerun outcomes rather than treating the stored v2 prefix calculation as a counterfactual replay.
Classify persistent reachability only on the diagnostic analysis side from paired conditioned lower/upper states; the controller remains unable to observe persistent state or hidden bounds.

Report overall success changes and changes restricted to target windows intersecting the paired persistent reachable interval. Do not count a noisy apparent admission outside that interval as evidence that the persistent target became reachable.
Compare one-pulse and adaptive controllers using total pulses, verify reads, reversals, apparent and persistent residuals, and target-conditioned failure probabilities.

Fit and validate the empirical kernel, the fourth-order Gaussian diagnostic, one global Uniform(-tau,+tau) baseline, and the predeclared target-conditioned eight-bin piecewise-uniform density. Use fit identities only, add a 0.5 pseudocount to each uniform bin, and apply the same held-out coverage and normalized target-binned Wasserstein gates to all compact candidates.

Linearly interpolate adjacent target-bin probability masses only for targets inside the characterized [0,1] grid. Reject targets outside that support by default; any target clamping and any endpoint clipping must be explicit and reported.

Sample corruption as an identity-level persistent mask and keep corrupt/stuck apparent and persistent terminal endpoints in a separate empirical inverse-CDF branch. For non-corrupt devices, first sample the paired-bound reachability class, then sample apparent success and apparent/persistent endpoints conditional on that class. Keep unreachable or budget-exhausted terminals out of the accepted-residual tail.
Compare the accepted 128-pulse apparent endpoints with Wan-2022 at one second in the common normalized coordinate and preserve the existing conductance-normalization and timing limitations.
